findings.summary: The residual panel's x axis is set to `-0.5 .. span + 0.5` with `span = max(int(trips[-1]), 1)`, so both figures run to active-set trip 15 while the plotted trajectory ends at trip 4. Eleven of sixteen slots are empty and the five real points are squeezed into under a third of the panel width, halving the resolution a reader has for the trip-1 rise that the frame-146 argument rests on.

The EFIT label flux contours are drawn in a very light grey that is hard to follow against white and noticeably fainter than the blue solved flux; where the two interleave in the poloidal panel the reference field a reader needs to compare against is the harder one to trace.

At the lower edge of the poloidal panel the red solved X-point cross and the red limiter-contact marker are drawn almost on top of each other, so a reader cannot separate the X-point from the contact point at the rendered scale, though the caption's bounding-surface reading does not depend on telling them apart.

Both figures place the poloidal panel at roughly a seventh of the canvas width, so the closed contours, the limiter outline and the solved-axis and X-point markers are drawn small relative to the space the legend and the wide residual axis consume; the panel is legible but the data the figure exists to show is the smallest element on the page.

notes: Both figures were judged only from the rendered PNGs named in the dispatch: image-0.png is frame 137 (the frame that holds its plasma) and image-1.png is frame 146 (the frame that loses it). No SVG was opened, read, listed, searched or parsed.

The two PNGs correspond to the run's committed panels at docs/figures/diiid-frame-146-vertical-loss/frame-137-flux-contours.svg and frame-146-flux-contours.svg on the reviewed head, which the run ships without PNG twins; the figure paths above name the PNG the reader is shown.

Finding anchoring: the residual-axis defect is reported against scripts/prototypes/diiid_forward_convergence/render_panels.py line 813, which the run reuses unchanged; the remaining findings are in the drawn artifact itself and carry a null line.

No blocking defect was found: no label is clipped or overlapping in frame 146, and in frame 137 the one near-collision is between two markers rather than between text, leaving every caption, legend entry and axis label readable.
This is a read-only figure review. No figure, caption or script was edited, moved or reformatted.
